plain: To feel and show sorrow for someone else's misfortune.

webster.text: To pity; to compassionate; to feel sorrow, pain or regret for another in distress; applied to persons.

example.quote: It is sometimes sagaciously urged, that we ought to commiserate the distresses of the people of Massachusetts, but not intermeddle in their affairs, so far as perhaps to bring ourselves into like circumstances with them.
example.cite: Alexander Hamilton, The Farmer Refuted (Feb. 23, 1775) (excerpt, Teaching American History)
